prize_parts.citation: For a visionary, densely patterned prose, rooted in poetry, that joins memory, the body and metaphysical dream into a singular imaginative architecture in Romanian.

statement.case_for: My configuration changes from Can Xue (B003) to Cărtărescu (B045). The reason is evidentiary and concerns sustained quality. In round 1 I wrote that if Can Xue's development could not be established, Cărtărescu might prove stronger on sustained quality. Nothing in the exchange establishes that development. Colleagues, and I myself, can say only that her method is consistent and unmistakable, and the file contains no evidence that the later books alter its terms. For Cărtărescu, public knowledge supports a voice recognizable within a page: long, rhythmically built, hallucinatory sentences that join memory, the body, the city and metaphysical speculation. It also supports a large, deliberate architecture across the Blinding (Orbitor) trilogy and Solenoid, with a poetic root. Sem-Sandberg's distinction persuades me. Recurrence of motif that is structural to a developing project differs from recurrence of method without development. This is the distinction I could not draw for Can Xue. It does not remove my reservation about economy, but it makes that reservation answerable on the book-by-book evidence. The case rests on the construction and language of the prose, not on post-communist context, reception or national symbolism. Can Xue remains, for me, among the most singular voices on the list, and my movement is a judgment about how much can be demonstrated, not a lowering of my regard for her work. The citation I propose credits the prose first and names poetry only as its root, because the prose has far better coverage in translation.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is the one I raised in round 1: the major novels are long and recurrent, and dense bodily and dream imagery can read as self-referential excess rather than depth. I cannot settle from public knowledge whether Solenoid and the later volumes sustain their length through variation. If a Romanian-language reader or an anonymous expert report finds that they rework earlier material, my change of position would not hold, and Can Xue or Carson would be the better choice. A second reservation is translation. The effect depends on syntactic density and rhythm in Romanian, which I can judge only through translation and general knowledge. A third is that the poetry and early work are unevenly covered, so the citation should not claim more breadth than the evidence supports. On the alternatives: Can Xue's case still turns on unproven development, and Carson's on the status of her translations and on how far her effects depend on book design.

responses.point: Sem-Sandberg distinguishes repetition of motif from repetition of method. He argues that Cărtărescu's recurring images are structural to a project that develops across volumes, whereas Can Xue's stable method raises the question of development. He would keep the citation tied to the large-scale prose, with poetry as a secondary strand.
responses.response: This distinction is the main reason I moved. In my round-1 reply you rightly noted that I could not answer the economy objection from the evidence, and I still cannot answer it fully. But a reservation about structural recurrence can be tested against the books, whereas a stable method with no demonstrated development leaves me with less to point to. I accept your scope: prose first, poetry as root, and nothing claimed for the early work beyond what readers of Romanian have assessed. I do not regard your point as proof that the late novels vary rather than repeat. It makes the claim defensible, not established.

responses.point: Mattson asked that the committee test Olsson's repetition point against Solenoid specifically. She said that if the later Can Xue shows real development she would regard her as a serious rival, and she keeps Can Xue as her first alternative.
responses.response: I take up your test and cannot complete it here. The record gives me no passage-level evidence on Solenoid, and I will not invent any. What I can say is that the test favors neither writer by default, because Can Xue's development is equally untested. I therefore now put the burden on the weaker-evidenced claim. You and I disagreed in round 1 on how much weight formal economy deserves. I still weigh it more than you do, but I no longer think it outweighs the evidence of architectural scale and development. Your openness to Can Xue is one I share, and she stays on my list of alternatives.

responses.point: Sward moved from Can Xue to Cărtărescu. She treats the open question of Can Xue's development as a real cost to her case, and she cautions that a citation naming poetry should be made only if readers have assessed it. She also stresses that the Romanian prose can be judged only through translation.
responses.response: I move for related but not identical reasons, and I do not take your move as an argument. I find your point about the poetry sound, and my citation therefore names it only as a root. On Can Xue, I agree that the sameness question has to be answered with evidence from the corpus, not with the assumption that consistency is depth. Where I differ is that I would still call that an open question and not a settled cost. A regional expert report on her Chinese prose could change my ranking back.

responses.point: Palm ranks Carson first and Can Xue third. She calls the question whether consistency of method is depth or limited range harder to settle for Can Xue than for Carson, and she is unsure that Carson's visual and material formats can be judged from the text alone.
responses.response: Your formulation of the dilemma stays with me and is part of why I changed. I accept that Autobiography of Red works as a text and that Carson's line-level control is real, so my earlier worry about book design applies mainly to Nox. The remaining difficulty for me is the scope of a whole-oeuvre citation when part of the corpus is translation and adaptation. I put Carson among my alternatives, not first, on that ground. Her case is a respectable one, and a citation resting on the original poetry, essay and hybrid forms would be defensible.

responses.point: Carlberg ranks Carson first by a narrower margin. She treats the recurrent concerns of desire, loss and the classical text as a method rather than a string of experiments, and she would draft the citation without mentioning translation.
responses.response: I accept that a compact, formally varied corpus can still show sustained quality, and I do not equate scale with depth, as you say. For me the difference is evidential: a large corpus offers more points at which sustained quality can be tested, and the question of Carson's durable core is one you also say needs checking against the whole bibliography. I would support the wording you propose if the committee prefers Carson, but I do not yet find it a stronger case than Cărtărescu's on the common criteria.

uncertainties: Whether the late Cărtărescu novels extend the project through variation or lapse into recurrent motifs. I have no passage-level evidence, and my change of position depends on this being answered favorably.

How much of the sentence-level effect in Romanian survives in translation, and how well translators have preserved the rhythm and syntax. A reader of the original or an anonymous regional expert report would help.
Whether the poetry and early prose can bear the weight of a citation. I limit it to naming poetry as the root.

Whether Can Xue's method develops across her large output, and whether the strangeness is built into her sentences or arises through critics' allegorical readings. I leave this open and have not resolved it against her.
Whether the weighting of sustained architectural scale against compact formal range, which now chiefly separates B045 and B004, is a matter of judgment on which members can reasonably differ.
I have not independently verified any text or source. My assessment rests on the supplied entries, the round-1 exchange and general public knowledge.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile. The profile records my scholarly work on the fragment, nihilism, exile literature and Celan, my poetry and translations, and my role as chair. These are context, not evidence of any connection to or preference for a shortlisted writer. As chair I was the sole explicit B003 supporter in round 1 and am now moving to B045. This is disclosed, not adjudicated, and I do not rest it on any support count. The profile records no documented connection to Cărtărescu, Can Xue, Carson or any other shortlisted writer.
